outcome.answer:
`parse` is implemented in `isodur.py`. All 54 tests pass; I ran them from the scratchpad, not the project directory.

The implementation is one anchored regex that enforces the unit order, the single `W` form, and the `T` structure. Two checks run after the match: a `T` with no time numbers after it is rejected, and a fraction is rejected on any number except the last one given. Years are 365 days and months are 30 days, as the docstring says.

The tests cover each rule and edge case the docstring names: the two docstring examples, both fraction separators, `P`, `PT`, `P1DT`, out-of-order and repeated units, signs, fractions on non-last numbers, `W` combined with other units, lower case, missing `P`, empty and whitespace-padded input, a trailing newline, numbers without a unit, and non-ASCII digits. They also check that non-`str` input raises `ValueError`. That last one is my choice; the docstring says "anything else raises ValueError", so I read it as covering that case.

The directory isn't a git repository, so I didn't commit anything.

{"file_path": "/tmp/agentdiff-haiku-bl9mynwx/work/isodur.py", "content": """"ISO 8601 durations, as seconds."""

import re

_NUM = r"([0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?)"
_DURATION = re.compile(
    rf"P(?:{_NUM}W|(?:{_NUM}Y)?(?:{_NUM}M)?(?:{_NUM}D)?(T(?:{_NUM}H)?(?:{_NUM}M)?(?:{_NUM}S)?)?)"
)
_YEAR = 365 * 86400
_MONTH = 30 * 86400
_WEEK = 7 * 86400
_DAY = 86400


def parse(text: str) -> float:
    """The number of seconds in an ISO 8601 duration such as ``P1DT2H30M`` or ``PT0.5S``.

    The form is ``P`` then optional ``nY``, ``nM``, ``nD``, then optionally ``T`` and optional ``nH``, ``nM``,
    ``nS``, in that order; or ``nW`` alone (``P2W``), with nothing else. A year is 365 days and a month 30 days.
    Numbers are digits, and only the last number given may have a fraction, written with ``.`` or ``,``
    (``PT1.5M``, ``P0,5D``). Upper case only. ``P`` alone, ``PT`` alone, a ``T`` with no time part after it,
    units out of order or repeated, a sign, a fraction on any number but the last, or anything else raises
    ValueError.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValueError(f"not an ISO 8601 duration: {text!r}")
    match = _DURATION.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"not an ISO 8601 duration: {text!r}")

    weeks, years, months, days, time_part, hours, minutes, seconds = match.group(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
    if time_part is not None and hours is None and minutes is None and seconds is None:
        raise ValueError(f"'T' with no time part: {text!r}")

    units = [
        (weeks, _WEEK),
        (years, _YEAR),
        (months, _MONTH),
        (days, _DAY),
        (hours, 3600),
        (minutes, 60),
        (seconds, 1),
    ]
    given = [value for value, _ in units if value is not None]
    if not given:
        raise ValueError(f"no components in duration: {text!r}")
    if any(("," in value or "." in value) for value in given[:-1]):
        raise ValueError(f"only the last number may have a fraction: {text!r}")

    return sum(float(value.replace(",", ".")) * size for value, size in units if value is not None)
"}
